physical_skill: Lift a full-size infusion pump by its carry handle, carry it back so the 25 mm pole enters its open 31 mm clamp throat, and hold it level at a tape band in free air against its off-axis weight while the other hand turns the clamp's lead-screw knob through about 3.4 turns in half-turn regrip strokes until the jaw bites; then both hands release and the pump must hang on its own clamp, upright, at the band, without sliding.
valid_shortcuts: None that score above 0.25: do nothing 0; one arm carries and lets go without turning the knob (drops down the pole, harm) 0; release after the first half turn (slides, harm) 0; screw the clamp tight while the pump stands on the table (5 cm low, not hanging) 0; keep holding the handle 0; clamped tight off the band 0.25 by design. Pushing the pump off the table or tipping it is harm (0). Distractors under the pump void hanging. Mass is reduced to 1.0 kg (disclosed), which makes the hold easier in simulation, not a different strategy.
distinct_from_nearest: No board task mounts a device on an IV pole or hangs a device by its own screw pole clamp. Nearest hold-while-fasten tasks (#2018, #3052, #1540) hold parts that are already constrained by a door, hinge or connector; here nothing constrains the pump until the jaw bites, so the holding hand carries the full off-axis load in air through a multi-stroke screw-up. The only pump task (#1966) loads tubing. Residual risks: reviewers may see it as another hold-while-fasten task, or question the 1.0 kg mass and table-mounted mast stand-in (both disclosed in fidelity and README).
